    "rationale": "Evidence: all nine designs ended off-track in all 60 trials. max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.066 m against the 0.06 m limit, and rms_error is about 0.03 m whatever the gain, speed or sensor span. Progress is almost fixed by track (oval about 0.12 to 0.17, s-bend about 0.04 to 0.07), so the robot drifts slowly off the line rather than failing on one sharp bend. Iteration 7 and 8 geometry (seven sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, 12 mm footprints, y = 0.06) gave the fewest line-loss events (1 per run), so I keep that geometry to isolate the controller.\n\nWhat I changed: the controller only. I raised kp from 1.2 to 2.5 so the proportional correction per metre of offset is about 62 per metre (slope 25/m times kp), giving about 220 PWM per cm of offset. This is well within saturation at base_speed 0.6. I raised ki from 0.3 to 2.0 to cancel the fixed left/right motor-mismatch bias faster. The integral stays limited to +/-2, so its maximum turn contribution is about 4 units (about 1400 PWM), which bounds windup. kd was lowered from 0.6 to 0.5 to avoid amplifying the faster response that the higher kp brings. base_speed stays at 0.6 so that the only changes are gain and bias correction. line_loss stays last_direction.\n\nWhy this test: iterations 1 to 8 varied kp from 1.2 to 3 at fixed ki, but kept ki at 0.3 or below and never moved ki well above that. A stronger integral is the untested way to remove a steady drift that proportional control alone leaves behind.\n\nExpected result: max_error below about 0.05 m, zero or one line-loss event per run, and progress above 0.2 on the development tracks. Completion within 3 s is unlikely at 0.6 base speed.
